items.quote: On the day that I ought to be afraid [of dangerous enemies], I put my trust in You.
items.text: No matter how hopeless your situation seems, trust in Hashem to take care of you, for you are always in His hands.

items.he: בֵּאלֹקִים בָּטַחְתִּי לֹא אִירָא מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה בָשָׂר לִי
items.quote: [Since] I trust in G-d I will not be afraid; what can mortal flesh do to me?

items.title: FOIL THEIR PLANS
items.he: יָגוּרוּ יִצְפּוֹנוּ הֵמָּה עֲקֵבַי יִשְׁמֹרוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר קִוּוּ נַפְשִׁי
items.quote: They gather and hide in ambush; they watch my every step, hoping [to take] my life.
items.text: My enemies are scheming against me because they cannot reconcile themselves to my existence. I depend upon You, Hashem, to foil their plans so that I can continue to survive.

items.he: עַל אָוֶן פַּלֶּט לָמוֹ בְּאַף עַמִּים הוֹרֵד אֱלֹקִים
items.quote: [This is] because of the [perceived] offense of escaping from them. O G-d, in Your anger take [the] peoples down [from their plans].

items.title: COUNT MY TEARS
items.he: שִׂימָה דִמְעָתִי בְנֹאדֶךָ הֲלֹא בְּסִפְרָתֶךָ
items.quote: Place my tears in Your flask [as well]. Are they not [also] in Your counting?
items.text: Ask Hashem to take an accounting of all the sufferings you have endured.

items.he: אָז יָשׁוּבוּ אוֹיְבַי אָחוֹר בְּיוֹם אֶקְרָא זֶה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי אֱלֹקִים לִי
items.quote: Then my foes will retreat on the day I cry out. [With] this I [will] know that G-d is with me.

items.title: BITACHON
items.he: בֵּאלֹקִים אֲהַלֵּל דָּבָר בַּה’ אֲהַלֵּל דָּבָר
items.quote: [When there are judgments] by G-d I will praise His word. [When there are kindnesses] by Hashem, I will praise His word.
items.text: Be ready to react trustingly to Hashem’s behavior towards you, whatever it may be, for you know He has your welfare in mind.

items.he: בֵּאלֹקִים בָּטַחְתִּי לֹא אִירָא מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אָדָם לִי
items.quote: In G-d I trust; I will not fear. What can man do to me?

items.title: YESHUAH
items.he: עָלַי אֱלֹקִים נְדָרֶיךָ אֲשַׁלֵּם תּוֹדֹת לָךְ
items.quote: Upon me is [the duty], O G-d, [to make good] my vows [of gratitude] to You. I will make thanksgiving offerings to You….
items.text: Be sure to express the gratitude you feel for having been saved by Hashem. Let your gratitude be as sincere as your plea to be saved.

items.he: כִּי הִצַּלְתָּ נַפְשִׁי מִמָּוֶת
items.quote: … because You rescued my soul from death.

57.title: Glory in a Cave
57.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: SEEKING SHELTER
items.he: וּבְצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ אֶחְסֶה עַד יַעֲבֹר הַוּוֹת
items.quote: And I will take refuge in the shelter of Your wings until the danger has passed.
items.text: Turn to Hashem for protection, especially when you are in personal danger.

items.title: MY FATE
items.he: אֶקְרָא לֵאלֹקִים עֶלְיוֹן לָאֵ־ל גֹּמֵר עָלָי
items.quote: I call upon G-d, Most High to the Almighty One Who decrees my fate.
items.text: Turn to Hashem in every situation of life for He is always in control.

items.title: ANGELS FROM ON HIGH
items.he: יִשְׁלַח מִשָּׁמַיִם וְיוֹשִׁיעֵנִי
items.quote: May G-d dispatch [His angels] from heaven and save me.
items.text: Ask Hashem to send His angels to save you from the vicious enemy.

items.title: AMID LIONS
items.he: נַפְשִׁי בְּתוֹךְ לְבָאִם
items.quote: My life is in the midst of lions.
items.text: Turn to Hashem for help because you are surrounded by lions and you are in fear of calling their attention to you.

items.title: NO LIMITS
items.he: רוּמָה עַל הַשָּׁמַיִם אֱלֹקִים עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדֶךָ
items.quote: You are higher than the heavens, O G-d. You will reveal Your glory to the entire world.
items.text: Hashem, when You save Yisrael You demonstrate that there are no limits to Your power.

items.he: כִּי גָדֹל עַד שָׁמַיִם חַסְדֶּךָ וְעַד שְׁחָקִים אֲמִתֶּךָ
items.quote: For Your kindness extends until the heavens and Your truth until the skies.
items.text: You also demonstrate that there is nothing within the entire universe that can interfere with Your qualities of kindness and truth.

items.title: HISTORY
items.he: כָּרוּ לְפָנַי שִׁיחָה נָפְלוּ בְתוֹכָהּ
items.quote: They dug a pit before me [but] they fell into it.
items.text: By saving Yisrael in the past Hashem has demonstrated His power.

items.title: STEADFAST
items.he: נָכוֹן לִבִּי אֱלֹקִים נָכוֹן לִבִּי אָשִׁירָה וַאֲזַמֵּרָה
items.quote: My heart is steadfast, O G-d, my heart is steadfast. [When You save me] I will sing and I will make music.
items.text: Yisrael will always be grateful for Hashem’s yeshuah.

items.title: AWAKEN
items.he: עוּרָה כְבוֹדִי עוּרָה הַנֵּבֶל וְכִנּוֹר אָעִירָה שָּׁחַר
items.quote: Awake, O my soul, awake! Awake, O lyre and harp! I will waken the dawn.
items.text: We begin our song of thanks even in the pre-dawn darkness when the signs of yeshuah are not yet visible.

items.title: ANTICIPATED THANKS
items.he: אוֹדְךָ בָעַמִּים אֲדֹ־נָי אֲזַמֶּרְךָ בַּלְאֻמִּים
items.quote: I will acknowledge my gratitude to You among the tribes, O L-rd. I will sing to You among the nations.
items.text: We look forward to publicly thanking Hashem for His yeshuah.

58.title: Against Complacency
58.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: SPEAK UP
items.he: הַאֻמְנָם אֵלֶם צֶדֶק תְּדַבֵּרוּן
items.quote: Are you indeed mute? You should be speaking [with] justice!
items.text: When you see an injustice being done you have an obligation to speak up. If you don’t take action, you are effectively complicit in the crime.

items.title: PATTERN OF EVIL
items.he: זֹרוּ רְשָׁעִים מֵרָחֶם
items.quote: The resha’im have deviated [early in their lives, as if] from birth.
items.text: A sinful pattern of behavior typically starts at an early age and becomes ingrained. This makes it all the more important to maintain effective guidance and discipline in raising children.

items.title: MELT AWAY
items.he: יִמָּאֲסוּ כְמוֹ מַיִם
items.quote: Let them melt away like water that runs off.
items.text: Ask Hashem to save you by gradually disabling your enemies, so that they will be like water that runs off.

items.he: כְּמוֹ שַׁבְּלוּל תֶּמֶס יַהֲלֹךְ
items.quote: [Let them disappear gradually] like the snail [appearing to] melt as it slithers away.

items.title: CHIZUK
items.he: יִשְׂמַח צַדִּיק כִּי חָזָה נָקָם
items.quote: The tzaddik will rejoice when he visualizes the vengeance [that will befall the rasha who does not mend his ways].
items.text: By visualizing the downfall of evil people your own emunah and bitachon will be strengthened.

items.he: וְיֹאמַר אָדָם אַךְ פְּרִי לַצַּדִּיק אַךְ יֵשׁ אֱלֹקִים שֹׁפְטִים בָּאָרֶץ
items.quote: And mankind will say, “There is indeed, a reward for the tzaddik. There is indeed, a G-d judging the earth.

59.title: Escape into the Night
59.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: ENEMIES
items.he: הַצִּילֵנִי מֵאֹיְבַי אֱלֹקָי מִמִּתְקוֹמְמַי תְּשַׂגְּבֵנִי
items.quote: Rescue me from my enemies, O my G-d. Defend me from my attackers.
items.text: Ask Hashem to save you from your enemies, whether they are motivated by hatred or self-interest.

items.he: הַצִּילֵנִי מִפֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן וּמֵאַנְשֵׁי דָמִים הוֹשִׁיעֵנִי
items.quote: Rescue me from evildoers. Save me from bloodthirsty men.

items.he: בְּלִי עָוֹן יְרוּצוּן וְיִכּוֹנָנוּ עוּרָה לִקְרָאתִי וּרְאֵה
items.quote: Without any wrongdoing [on my part] they are hurrying and preparing [to kill me]. Rise up for me and see [what is in their hearts].

items.title: JUDGMENT
items.he: הָקִיצָה לִפְקֹד כָּל הַגּוֹיִם
items.quote: Arise to pass judgement against all nations [who seek to harm Yisrael].
items.text: Even if I am unable to defend myself, let Your judgment take its toll of those who are guilty.

items.he: עֻזּוֹ, אֵלֶיךָ אֶשְׁמֹרָה כִּי אֱלֹקִים מִשְׂגַּבִּי
items.quote: [In the face of the enemy’s] strength, I wait for You, for G-d is my stronghold.

items.title: STRENGTH AND KINDNESS
items.he: וַאֲנִי אָשִׁיר עֻזֶּךָ וַאֲרַנֵּן לַבֹּקֶר חַסְדֶּךָ
items.quote: But as for me I will sing of Your strength, and exult in Your kindness every morning.
items.text: Thank Hashem for using His strength to keep the enemy away from you and for using His kindness to enable you to escape harm.

items.he: עֻזִּי אֵלֶיךָ אֲזַמֵּרָה כִּי אֱלֹקִים מִשְׂגַּבִּי אֱלֹקֵי חַסְדִּי
items.quote: You are my strength, I will sing [in praise] to You, that G-d is my stronghold and the G-d of my welfare.

60.title: Hashgachah in Wartime
60.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: ABANDONED
items.he: אֱלֹקִים זְנַחְתָּנוּ, פְרַצְתָּנוּ אָנַפְתָּ תְּשׁוֹבֵב לָנוּ
items.quote: O G-d. You have abandoned us. You have made us defenseless. You have become furious [because of our sins]. Return to us.
items.text: Plead with Hashem to restore His relationship with us. The reverses we have recently experienced are an indication that He has temporarily abandoned us and this must have been due to our sins

items.he: הִרְאִיתָה עַמְּךָ קָשָׁה, הִשְׁקִיתָנוּ יַיִן תַּרְעֵלָה
items.quote: You have shown Your nation a harsh [spectacle], You made us drink the wine of stupefaction.

items.he: הֲלֹא אַתָּה אֱלֹקִים זְנַחְתָּנוּ, וְלֹא תֵצֵא אֱלֹקִים בְּצִבְאוֹתֵינוּ
items.quote: You have forsaken us and You do not go forth, O G-d, with our legions.

items.title: RIGHT HAND
items.he: לְמַעַן יֵחָלְצוּן יְדִידֶיךָ, הוֹשִׁיעָה יְמִינְךָ וַעֲנֵנִי
items.quote: In order that Your beloved ones may be released [from servitude to the enemy], save them with Your right hand and answer me.
items.text: Ask Hashem to bring to bear the power of His right hand so that we will be saved from the depredations of the enemy.

items.title: UNRELIABLE ALLIES
items.he: הָבָה לָּנוּ עֶזְרָת מִצָּר, וְשָׁוְא תְּשׁוּעַת אָדָם
items.quote: Give us help against the foe, for human help is futile.
items.text: We cannot rely upon the help of nations which are inconstant and act in their own perceived self-interest.

items.he: בֵּאלֹקִים נַעֲשֶׂה חָיִל, וְהוּא יָבוּס צָרֵינוּ
items.quote: [We pray that] through G-d we will act valiantly and He will trample our foes.

61.title: To Dwell in Your Tent
61.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: TO HEAR
items.he: שִׁמְעָה אֱלֹקִים רִנָּתִי הַקְשִׁיבָה תְּפִלָּתִי
items.quote: Hear, O G-d, my song of praise and supplication. Listen to my [silent] prayer.
items.text: Ask Hashem to take note of your tefillos in whatever form they may be.

items.title: FROM AFAR
items.he: מִקְצֵה הָאָרֶץ אֵלֶיךָ אֶקְרָא
items.quote: From the end of the land, I call to You.
items.text: Call to Hashem in prayer no matter where you are, for He is everywhere.

items.title: SHELTER
items.he: בַּעֲטֹף לִבִּי בְּצוּר יָרוּם מִמֶּנִּי תַנְחֵנִי
items.quote: When my heart grows faint, You lead me to a rock that soars above me.
items.text: Call to Hashem no matter what your circumstances, for He will give you shelter.

items.he: כִּי הָיִיתָ מַחְסֶה לִי מִגְדַּל עֹז מִפְּנֵי אוֹיֵב
items.quote: For You have [always] been a refuge for me, a tower of strength in the face of the enemy.

items.title: SANCTUARY
items.he: אָגוּרָה בְאָהָלְךָ עוֹלָמִים
items.quote: Let me dwell in Your tent forever.
items.text: Ask Hashem to enable you to live in an environment where you can be close to Him.

items.he: יֵשֵׁב עוֹלָם לִפְנֵי אֱלֹקִים
items.quote: May he sit forever before G-d.

items.raw: [61:7] LIFE. – יָמִים עַל יְמֵי מֶלֶךְ תּוֹסִיף שְׁנוֹתָיו כְּמוֹ דֹר וָדֹר – May You add days onto the days of the king (i.e. David). May his years be like all generations.” Ask Hashem to let you live out your years in good health so that you can serve Him and complete your life’s mission.
[61:9] HIS NAME. – כֵּן אֲזַמְּרָה שִׁמְךָ לָעַד – So will I sing Your Name forever.” Reflect upon the wondrous attributes of Hashem, as represented by His Name.

items.he: חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת מַן יִנְצְרֻהוּ
items.quote: Designate [Hashem’s] kindness and truth to guard him (i.e. David).

62.title: Practicing Patience
62.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: BE PATIENT
items.he: אַךְ אֶל אֱלֹקִים דּוּמִיָּה נַפְשִׁי, מִמֶּנּוּ יְשׁוּעָתִי
items.quote: My soul is quietly waiting, but only for G-d. My yeshuah comes from Him.
items.text: Even when your problems are overwhelming, be patient because your yeshuah can come only from Hashem. Reckless steps that you might be tempted to take will only make things worse.

items.he: אַךְ הוּא צוּרִי וִישׁוּעָתִי מִשְׂגַּבִּי לֹא אֶמּוֹט
items.quote: He alone is my Rock and my Yeshuah; my Stronghold, I will not stumble.
items.text: Don’t be deceitful toward those in lawful authority.

items.he: עַל אֱלֹקִים יִשְׁעִי
items.quote: Upon G-d rests my yeshuah.

items.title: BE HONEST
items.he: יִרְצוּ כָזָב בְּפִיו יְבָרֵכוּ וּבְקִרְבָּם יְקַלְלוּ
items.quote: They take pleasure in deceit, blessing me with the mouth, but on the inside they curse me.
items.text: Don’t be deceitful toward those in lawful authority.

items.title: DO TESHUVAH WITH ALL YOUR HEART
items.he: שִׁפְכוּ לְפָנָיו לְבַבְכֶם
items.quote: Pour out your hearts before Him.
items.text: Do teshuvah and ask Hashem to bring the Geulah, but do it sincerely, with all your heart.

items.title: HIS STRENGTH
items.he: אַחַת דִּבֶּר אֱלֹקִים שְׁתַּיִם זוּ שָׁמָעְתִּי כִּי עֹז לֵאלֹקִים
items.quote: One thing has G-d spoken, I have heard these two [things]: that strength belongs to G-d.
items.text: Hashem exercises His strength to punish the wicked.

items.title: HIS KINDNESS
items.he: וּלְךָ אֲדֹ־נָי חָסֶד כִּי אַתָּה תְשַׁלֵּם לְאִישׁ כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ
items.quote: and Yours, Hashem, is kindness, for You repay each man according to his deeds.
items.text: Because of His kindness, Hashem rewards righteousness to thousands of generations.

63.title: Transcending Fear
63.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: CRISIS
items.he: מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד בִּהְיוֹתוֹ בְּמִדְבַּר יְהוּדָה
items.quote: A Mizmor by David, when he was in the wilderness of Yehudah.
items.text: Even when your survival is at stake, don’t abandon your focus on serving Hashem. In fact, your bond with Hashem will strengthen you and help you deal with the crisis.

items.title: SEEKING
items.he: אֱלֹקִים אֵ־לִי אַתָּה אֲשַׁחֲרֶךָּ
items.quote: O G-d, You Are my G-d. I seek You.
items.text: Develop a personal relationship with Hashem.

items.title: HOLINESS
items.he: כָּמַהּ לְךָ בְשָׂרִי
items.quote: My flesh thirsts for You.
items.text: Absorb holiness into your body by focusing on Hashem when you do mitzvos.

items.he: כֵּן אֲבָרֶכְךָ בְחַיָּי בְּשִׁמְךָ אֶשָּׂא כַפָּי
items.quote: Then, I will bless You with my life. I will lift my hands [to] Your Name.

items.title: SPIRITUAL EXISTENCE
items.he: כִּי טוֹב חַסְדְּךָ מֵחַיִּים שְׂפָתַי יְשַׁבְּחוּנְךָ
items.quote: Because Your kindness is better than life, my lips will praise You.
items.text: Thank Hashem for giving you a spiritual existence that enables you to perceive Him.

items.title: WINGS
items.he: כִּי הָיִיתָ עֶזְרָתָה לִּי וּבְצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ אֲרַנֵּן
items.quote: For You are my help and so I joyously sing to You under the shade of your protective wings.
items.text: Thank Hashem for protecting you.

64.title: Counsellors of Bitterness
64.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: MY VOICE
items.he: שְׁמַע אֱלֹקִים קוֹלִי בְשִׂיחִי
items.quote: O G-d, Hear my voice as I speak.
items.text: When you ask Hashem’s help, let your voice be heard, at least to yourself. It is not enough just to think your plea.

items.title: THREAT
items.he: מִפַּחַד אוֹיֵב תִּצֹּר חַיָּי
items.quote: Guard my life from the fear of the enemy.
items.text: Ask Hashem to disable the power of those who threaten you so that you need not live in fear.

items.title: CONSPIRACIES
items.he: תַּסְתִּירֵנִי מִסּוֹד מְרֵעִים מֵרִגְשַׁת פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן
items.quote: Shield me from the secret gathering of evil men, from the public assemblage of evildoers.
items.text: Ask Hashem to prevent the schemes of your enemies from becoming a reality.

items.title: BITTERNESS
items.he: אֲשֶׁר שָׁנְנוּ כַחֶרֶב לְשׁוֹנָם דָּרְכוּ חִצָּם דָּבָר מָר
items.quote: They have sharpened their tongue like the sword and have aimed a bitter word as their arrow.
items.text: Express your anguish to Hashem at the bitterness being demonstrated against you by those who hate you. Perhaps if Hashem sees your suffering, He will have pity on you.

items.title: RETRIBUTION
items.he: וַיֹּרֵם אֱלֹקִים חֵץ, פִּתְאוֹם הָיוּ מַכּוֹתָם
items.quote: But G-d will shoot the arrow [of retribution] at them. They will be suddenly struck down.
items.text: Trust Hashem to take retribution aginst the perpetrators of evil.

items.title: RETRIBUTION
items.he: וַיַּכְשִׁילוּהוּ עָלֵימוֹ לְשׁוֹנָם יִתְנֹדֲדוּ כָּל רֹאֵה בָם
items.quote: Their own tongue will trip them up. All who see them will recoil [in shock].
items.text: Hashem invokes retribution in a way that demonstrates His power and His wisdom.

items.title: ALL MEN
items.he: וַיִּירְאוּ כָּל אָדָם וַיַּגִּידוּ פֹּעַל אֱלֹקִים וּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ הִשְׂכִּילוּ
items.quote: Then all men will be awed and they will declare it is G-d’s doing. They will comprehend His action.
items.text: The people of the world will ultimately declare the greatness of Hashem, for the evidence of His power will be clear to all.

items.title: TZADIKIM
items.he: יִשְׂמַח צַדִּיק בַּה’ וְחָסָה בוֹ וְיִתְהַלְלוּ כָּל יִשְׁרֵי לֵב
items.quote: The tzadik will rejoice in [gratitude to] Hashem and take refuge in Him. All who are upright in heart will exult.
items.text: Seek to be one of those tzadikim who exult in relying totally upon Hashem. Their exultation expresses their gratitude and relief at being vindicated by Hashem’s actions.

65.title: A Celebration of Rain
65.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: STUNNED AWE
items.he: לְךָ דֻמִיָּה תְהִלָּה
items.quote: Silence is [the only suitable] praise to You.
items.text: You should feel a stunned awe in the presence of Hashem, an awe that makes it difficult for you to take it upon yourself to praise Him.

items.title: TZION
items.he: אֱלֹקִים בְּצִיּוֹן
items.quote: [You are] G-d in Tzion.
items.text: Although G-d’s presence fills the entire universe, He has chosen Tzion as a special focus.

items.title: VOWS
items.he: וּלְךָ יְשֻׁלַּם נֶדֶר
items.quote: to You will vows be paid.
items.text: Despite the unlimited greatness of Hashem He has chosen to accept mankind’s payments in fulfillment of vows, accompanied by sincere prayer.

items.title: PRAYER
items.he: שֹׁמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה עָדֶיךָ כָּל בָּשָׂר יָבֹאוּ
items.quote: [You are the] One that hears prayer. All mankind may come to You.
items.text: Although G-d’s power is unlimited, He is concerned with the prayers of each person.

items.title: TO THE ENDS OF THE EARTH
items.he: מִבְטָח כָּל קַצְוֵי אֶרֶץ וְיָם רְחֹקִים
items.quote: [You are the] trustworthy Refuge [to] all the ends of the earth and the far off seas.
items.text: No matter where you are, in the farthest regions of the earth, you can be close to Hashem.

items.title: VEGETATION AND RAIN
items.he: מֵכִין הָרִים בְּכֹחוֹ נֶאְזָר בִּגְבוּרָה
items.quote: [You are He Who] sets mountains with [rich vegetation], [and Who is] girded with might.
items.text: All the wonders of nature are the work of Hashem, provided for the benefit of mankind. We should aspire to be worthy of His kindness.

items.title: RESTRAINT
items.he: מַשְׁבִּיחַ שְׁאוֹן יַמִּים שְׁאוֹן גַּלֵּיהֶם
items.quote: [You are He Who] calms the roar of the seas, the roar of their waves.
items.text: The greatness of Hashem is revealed, not so much in the massive power He wields, but in His ability to control and restrain that power. This is an important lesson for mankind — the art of self-restraint.

items.title: GUILT
items.he: דִּבְרֵי עֲוֹנֹת גָּבְרוּ מֶנִּי פְּשָׁעֵינוּ אַתָּה תְכַפְּרֵם
items.quote: The consequences of sins have overwhelmed me. [Yet] You forgive our transgressions.
items.text: You should feel overwhelming guilt because of your sins against Hashem. But that still shouldn’t stop you from turning to Him and begging forgiveness.

items.title: NEARNESS
items.he: אַשְׁרֵי תִּבְחַר וּתְקָרֵב
items.quote: Fortunate is He Whom You choose and bring near.
items.text: Aspire to achieve spiritual closeness to Hashem and ask Him to help you towards this goal.

66.title: A Celebration of Yeshuah
66.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: DREAMS FULFILLED
items.he: הָרִיעוּ לֵאלֹקִים כָּל הָאָרֶץ
items.quote: Hail G-d with a joyful salute, all [you peoples of] the earth!
items.text: This part of the mizmor is directed to the nations of the world but the Jewish people will experience special joy in publicy acclaiming Hashem and seeing their dreams fulfilled.

items.raw: [66:2] – זַמְּרוּ כְבוֹד שְׁמוֹ שִׂימוּ כָבוֹד תְּהִלָּתוֹ: – Sing of the glory of His Name. Render glory [by singing] His praise.

[66:5] HISTORY. – לְכוּ וּרְאוּ מִפְעֲלוֹת אֱלֹקִים – [Let Jews say to each other:] “Come and see the works of G-d. Awesome is [His] methodology [of control] over [the history of] mankind.” Recall the events by which Hashem guided the history of national development for us and the nations of the world.
[66:6] – הָפַךְ יָם לְיַבָּשָׁה בַּנָּהָר יַעַבְרוּ בְרָגֶל – He turned the Sea into dry land. They crossed the River on foot [to enter Eretz Yisrael]. There we will rejoice in Him.

items.title: FIRE AND WATER
items.he: בָּאנוּ בָאֵשׁ וּבַמַּיִם וַתּוֹצִיאֵנוּ לָרְוָיָה
items.quote: We came through fire and water. [But now] You brought us out to abundance.
items.text: Thank Hashem for the abundance you are enjoying. Even your tribulations of “fire and water” were of value to you because of their effect upon your character. Your appreciation of good fortune is directly dependent upon what you went through to get where you are now.

items.title: OFFERINGS
items.he: אָבוֹא בֵיתְךָ בְעוֹלוֹת אֲשַׁלֵּם לְךָ נְדָרָי
items.quote: [Hashem,] I shall come into Your House with burnt-offerings. I shall fulfill my vows to You.
items.text: Look forward to the opportunity to demonstrate your gratitude to Hashem in a concrete, physical way.

items.title: DISTRACTIONS
items.he: אָוֶן אִם רָאִיתִי בְלִבִּי לֹא יִשְׁמַע אֲדֹ־נָי
items.quote: [Even] if I had allowed [thoughts of] iniquity in my heart, Hashem would not have listened.
items.text: Even if your tefillos to Hashem were marred by distractions, thoughts that you found difficult to control, Hashem heard your good thoughts and disregarded the thoughts you did not really mean to have.

items.title: ATTENTION
items.he: בָּרוּךְ אֱלֹקִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא הֵסִיר תְּפִלָּתִי וְחַסְדּוֹ מֵאִתִּי
items.quote: Blessed is G-d, Who has not turned away my prayer nor His lovingkindness from me.
items.text: Thank Hashem for giving you His individual attention when you pray to Him. Even if you are unworthy, He loves you and listens to your tefillos in every situation that you may find yourself.

67.title: A Blessing to the World
67.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: SOURCE OF BLESSING
items.he: לַמְנַצֵּחַ בִּנְגִינֹת מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר
items.quote: For the musician, with musical accompaniment, a mizmor, a song.
items.text: Because of its symbolic significance many authorities recommend reciting this entire mizmor daily with sincere concentration. (In fact it appears as part of the daily Pesukei D’Zimrah according to Nusach Sfard)

items.title: FLOW OF BLESSING
items.he: אֱלֹקִים יְחָנֵּנוּ וִיבָרְכֵנוּ יָאֵר פָּנָיו אִתָּנוּ
items.quote: May G-d find favor in us. May He bless us, and shine His countenance upon us.
items.text: Ask Hashem to let the flow of His blessing pass to your family and all of Yisrael.

notes: It is written in the name of the Maharshal that when a person recites this mizmor in the presence of the menorah in shul at sunrise, it is as though he had kindled the Menorah in the Bais Hamikdash. Having this in mind will protect him from any harsh edict and will assure him a place in the World to Come.

items.title: THE LIGHT OF KNOWLEDGE
items.he: לָדַעַת בָּאָרֶץ דַּרְכֶּךָ בְּכָל גּוֹיִם יְשׁוּעָתֶךָ
items.quote: To make known Your way on earth, [to demonstrate] Your yeshuah to all nations.
items.text: Ask Hashem to bring the Geulah so that all nations will serve Hashem and live at peace with each other.

120.title: Victimized by Lies
120.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah, expressing your devotion to Hashem.

items.title: IN DISTRESS
items.he: בַּצָּרָתָה לִּי קָרָאתִי וַיַּעֲנֵנִי
items.quote: [I turned] to Hashem when I was in dire distress [Whenever] I called upon him, He answered me.
items.text: Even if the intensity of your tefillah only rises to a high level when you are in dire distress, don’t be reluctant to call upon Him for help at any time.

items.title: VICTIMIZED BY SLANDER
items.he: ה’ הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שֶׁקֶר מִלָּשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה
items.quote: Hashem, rescue my soul from false lips, a deceitful tongue.
items.text: If you have become the object of slanderous accusations, appeal to Hashem to save you and clear your name.

items.title: THE EVIL OF SLANDER
items.he: מַה יִּתֵּן לְךָ וּמַה יֹּסִיף לָךְ לָשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה
items.quote: You slanderer, what does a deceitful tongue give to you and what value does it add [to your life]?
items.text: Think carefully before committing the sin of harming another person’s reputation through slanderous or gossiping talk.

items.title: EXILE
items.he: אוֹיָה לִי כִּי גַרְתִּי מֶשֶׁךְ
items.quote: Woe unto me for I have dwelled in a drawn-out [exile].
items.text: Acknowledge the pain the Jewish people has suffered in this Exile, and plead with Hashem to relieve it.

items.title: A BITTER FOE
items.he: רַבַּת שָׁכְנָה לָּהּ נַפְשִׁי עִם שׂוֹנֵא שָׁלוֹם
items.quote: Too long has my soul dwelled with those who hate peace.
items.text: Ask Hashem for peace.

items.he: אֲנִי שָׁלוֹם וְכִי אֲדַבֵּר הֵמָּה לַמִּלְחָמָה
items.quote: I [seek] peace but when I speak [to them], they are for war.

121.title: “I Lift My Eyes”
121.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah asking for your needs, or expressing your gratitude and devotion to Hashem.

items.title: HELP
items.he: עֶזְרִי מֵעִם ה’ עֹשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ
items.quote: My help is from Hashem, Maker of heaven and earth.
items.text: When you are faced with difficulties, look to Hashem. He created the world you live in and He is the only One Who can help you.

items.title: ALWAYS THERE
items.he: הִנֵּה לֹא יָנוּם וְלֹא יִישָׁן שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל
items.quote: Indeed, He does not slumber and He does not sleep, the Guardian of Yisrael.
items.text: You can be sure that Hashem is watching over you every minute of the day. Even when you are asleep, He is awake.

items.title: UNIVERSAL PROTECTION
items.he: ה’ יִשְׁמָרְךָ מִכָּל רָע יִשְׁמֹר אֶת נַפְשֶׁךָ
items.quote: Hashem protects you from every evil. He protects your soul.
items.text: Hashem protects you from being swept away by cultural influences.

items.title: ETERNAL PROTECTION
items.he: ה’ יִשְׁמָר צֵאתְךָ וּבוֹאֶךָ מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם
items.quote: Hashem watches over your departure and your arrival, from now and forever.
items.text: Hashem will always be there to protect you, even when you are far away from home, even when you are enduring the sufferings of Exile.

122.title: Remembered Glory
122.intro: Listed below are some of the lessons that you can draw from this mizmor, as well as some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah to Hashem.

items.title: THE HOUSE OF HASHEM
items.he: שָׂמַחְתִּי בְּאֹמְרִים לִי בֵּית ה’ נֵלֵךְ:
items.quote: I rejoiced when they said to me, ‘Let us go to the House of Hashem.’
items.text: The Bais HaMikdash is the place where the greatness of Hashem as Master of the universe is most clearly perceived. It is there that the intensity of His presence is most felt and so it is there that Hashem is seen as truly great.

items.title: THE CITY OF HASHEM
items.he: יְרוּשָׁלַ ִם הַבְּנוּיָה כְּעִיר שֶׁחֻבְּרָה לָּהּ יַחְדָּו:
items.quote: Yerushalayim, massively built, like a city to which [people of the distant regions] come together.
items.text: The City of Hashem is the place which people of distant regions come together in brotherhood and goodwill.

items.title: A TESTIMONY FOR YISRAEL
items.he: עֵדוּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְהֹדוֹת לְשֵׁם ה’
items.quote: a testimony for Yisrael, to give thanks to the Name of Hashem.
items.text: The miracles that occurred in Yerushalayim were a testimony for Yisrael, that the Shechinah dwells within the nation. Yerushalayim was seen to absorb all 12 tribes and yet they did not feel cramped.

items.title: RESTORATION
items.he: כִּי שָׁמָּה יָשְׁבוּ כִסְאוֹת לְמִשְׁפָּט כִּסְאוֹת לְבֵית דָּוִיד:
items.quote: For there sat [wise men on] the seats of judgment [and] the thrones of the house of David.
items.text: Ask Hashem to bring the Geulah (Redemption), restore the Sanhedrin, rebuild Yerusahayim, and establish again the reign of the House of David.

items.title: PEACE
items.he: שַׁאֲלוּ שְׁלוֹם יְרוּשָׁלָ ִם יִשְׁלָיוּ אֹהֲבָיִךְ
items.quote: Pray for the peace of Yerushalayim: “Let those who love you, [O Yerushayim,] enjoy the tranquility.
items.text: Ask Hashem to restore the peace of Yerushalayim.

items.he: יְהִי שָׁלוֹם בְּחֵילֵךְ שַׁלְוָה בְּאַרְמְנוֹתָיִךְ
items.quote: May there be be peace within your outer defenses; may there be tranquility in your inner citadels.

123.title: An End to Contempt
123.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: ON HIGH
items.he: אֵלֶיךָ נָשָׂאתִי אֶת עֵינַי הַיֹּשְׁבִי בַּשָּׁמָיִם
items.quote: I have raised my eyes to You, Who dwells in the heavens.
items.text: Hashem is described as dwelling on high. This signifies that He is unaffected by the viciousness and corruption of sinful human beings on earth. However, He observes all and is ready to intervene when the time right.

items.title: SUBMISSIVENESS
items.he: הִנֵּה כְעֵינֵי עֲבָדִים אֶל יַד אֲדוֹנֵיהֶם
items.quote: Behold! Like the eyes of servants to their master’s hand.
items.text: To ask for Hashem’s favor, you need to be totally humble and submissive to Him. Don’t take the attitude that He owes you.

items.title: SMUGNESS
items.he: רַבַּת שָׂבְעָה לָּהּ נַפְשֵׁנוּ הַלַּעַג הַשַּׁאֲנַנִּים
items.quote: Too long has our soul been sated with the mockery of the [nations who are] complacent in their smugness.
items.text: Avoid the complacency of which our enemies are guilty.

items.title: END OF CONTEMPT
items.he: חָנֵּנוּ ה’ חָנֵּנוּ כִּי רַב שָׂבַעְנוּ בוּז
items.quote: Favor us, Hashem, favor us for [the Exile] has been very long. We have become fully sated with contempt.
items.text: Humbly ask Hashem to teach the nations that it is not in their interest to deride us.

124.title: The Bird Has Escaped!
124.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: THE BEASTS
items.he: אֲזַי חַיִּים בְּלָעוּנוּ בַּחֲרוֹת אַפָּם בָּנוּ
items.quote: Then they would have swallowed us alive when their fury raged against us.
items.text: Thank Hashem for saving us from wicked men eager to expend their fury and hatred against us.

items.he: לוּלֵי ה’ שֶׁהָיָה לָנוּ בְּקוּם עָלֵינוּ אָדָם
items.quote: Were it not for Hashem, Who was for us, [there would have been no one to help us] when a man [Haman] rose against us.

items.title: THE FLOODS
items.he: אֲזַי הַמַּיִם שְׁטָפוּנוּ נַחְלָה עָבַר עַל נַפְשֵׁנוּ
items.quote: Then the [flood] waters would have overwhelmed us; [the] torrent would have swept over our life.
items.text: Thank Hashem for saving us from all kinds of natural disasters and economic difficulties.

items.he: אֲזַי עָבַר עַל נַפְשֵׁנוּ הַמַּיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים
items.quote: Then there would have swept over our lives — the maliciously churning waters.

items.title: THE TRAP
items.he: הַפַּח נִשְׁבָּר וַאֲנַחְנוּ נִמְלָטְנוּ
items.quote: the trap was broken and we escaped.
items.text: Thank Hashem for saving us from difficult situations from which there seemed no escape.

items.title: THE METAPHOR
items.he: נַפְשֵׁנוּ כְּצִפּוֹר נִמְלְטָה מִפַּח יוֹקְשִׁים
items.quote: Our life is like a bird escaped from the hunter’s trap.
items.text: Don’t let yourself be depressed by a difficult situation in life. Follow David’s example and visualize your difficulty with a metaphor that will help you see how Hashem’s help is on the way.

items.title: HELP
items.he: עֶזְרֵנוּ בְּשֵׁם ה’ עֹשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ
items.quote: Our help is by [calling upon] the Name of Hashem, Maker of heaven and earth.
items.text: In every challenge of life, whether it is of human origin, a natural disaster, or other threat, call upon Hashem to help you for there is nothing that is beyond His ability to control.

125.title: A Mountain of Trust
125.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: THE MOUNTAIN
items.he: הַבֹּטְחִים בַּה’ כְּהַר צִיּוֹן לֹא יִמּוֹט, לְעוֹלָם יֵשֵׁב
items.quote: Those who trust in Hashem [will be secure] like Har Tzion, [that is] immovable, sitting [on its base] forever.
items.text: Work on your bitachon by visualizing it as a mountain, knowing that you will be secure in Hashem’s care.

items.title: THE NATION
items.he: יְרוּשָׁלַ ִם הָרִים סָבִיב לָהּ, וַה’ סָבִיב לְעַמּוֹ מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם
items.quote: Yerushalayim has [protective] mountains around it. [So will] Hashem be round about his people, now and forever.
items.text: Hashem protects His nation of Yisrael and His protection will continue for all time, like the permanence of the mountains around Yerushalayim.

items.title: THE RIGHTEOUS
items.he: הֵיטִיבָה ה’ לַטּוֹבִים וְלִישָׁרִים בְּלִבּוֹתָם
items.quote: Do good, Hashem, to the good and to the upright of heart.
items.text: Ask Hashem to grant a special measure of well-being to the tzaddikim of your generation, for the world exists in their zechus.

126.title: It was a Bad Dream
126.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: A DREAM
items.he: בְּשׁוּב ה’ אֶת שִׁיבַת צִיּוֹן הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים
items.quote: When Hashem brings [us] back [from] the captivity of Tzion, we will be like dreamers [who have woken up].
items.text: Even if things seem bleak now, remember that the Geulah will surely come.

items.title: LAUGHTER
items.he: אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ וּלְשׁוֹנֵנוּ רִנָּה
items.quote: Then our mouths will be filled with laughter.
items.text: Full-throated joy is reserved for the time of the Geulah. Only then will our mouths be filled with laughter.

items.title: GREAT THINGS
items.he: אָז יֹאמְרוּ בַגּוֹיִם הִגְדִּיל ה’ לַעֲשׂוֹת עִם אֵלֶּה
items.quote: Then they will talk among the nations [saying], Hashem has done great things for these [people].
items.text: Encourage the nations to acknowledge the greatness of Hashem.

items.title: OUR RESPONSE
items.he: הִגְדִּיל ה’ לַעֲשׂוֹת עִמָּנוּ הָיִינוּ שְׂמֵחִים
items.quote: Hashem has done great [things] for us. We were [already] gladdened.

items.title: TO FLOW AGAIN
items.he: שׁוּבָה ה’ אֶת שְׁבִיתֵנוּ כַּאֲפִיקִים בַּנֶּגֶב
items.quote: Hashem, bring back our capitivity as streams of running water in the desert.
items.text: After each meal, thank Hashem and ask Him to bring the Geulah now.

127.title: To Build the House
127.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: BUILDING IT
items.he: אִם ה’ לֹא יִבְנֶה בַיִת שָׁוְא עָמְלוּ בוֹנָיו
items.quote: If Hashem does not build a house, in vain do its builders labor over it.
items.text: Put your efforts into doing what is right, but always keep in mind that what actually happens depends on the will of Hashem.

items.title: YOUR EFFORT
items.he: שָׁוְא לָכֶם מַשְׁכִּימֵי קוּם מְאַחֲרֵי שֶׁבֶת אֹכְלֵי לֶחֶם הָעֲצָבִים
items.quote: In vain, you who rise [extra] early, [you] who sit up late, [and you who] eat the bread of miserable drudgery.
items.text: Don’t lose yourself in hishtadlus (personal effort), expending time and energy on material things at the expense of avodas Hashem.

items.title: WORTHY CHILDREN
items.he: נַחֲלַת ה’ בָּנִים שָׂכָר פְּרִי הַבָּטֶן
items.quote: the legacy of Hashem is children. The fruit of the womb is a [great] reward.
items.text: Ask Hashem to bless you with worthy children.

128.title: The Virtuous Life
128.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: HAPPINESS
items.he: אַשְׁרֵי כָּל יְרֵא ה’ הַהֹלֵךְ בִּדְרָכָיו
items.quote: Fortunate is every person who fears Hashem and who walks in His ways.
items.text: Consider yourself fortunate to live a virtuous life. It is the secret to happiness.

items.title: WOMAN IS THE HEART
items.he: אֶשְׁתְּךָ כְּגֶפֶן פֹּרִיָּה בְּיַרְכְּתֵי בֵיתֶךָ
items.quote: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine in the inner chambers of your home.
items.text: Respect your wife for she is the heart of your home.

items.title: BLESSING
items.he: כִי כֵן יְבֹרַךְ גָּבֶר יְרֵא ה’
items.quote: Indeed, for so will the man be blessed who fears Hashem.
items.text: The fear of Hashem is the secret to a blessed existence.

items.title: WORK
items.he: יְגִיעַ כַּפֶּיךָ כִּי תֹאכֵל אַשְׁרֶיךָ וְטוֹב לָךְ
items.quote: When you eat the labor of your hands, you will be happy and it will be good for you.
items.text: Don’t live beyond your means.

items.title: TZION
items.he: יְבָרֶכְךָ ה’ מִצִּיּוֹן וּרְאֵה בְּטוּב יְרוּשָׁלָ ִם כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ
items.quote: May Hashem bless you from Tzion. May you witness the good fortune of Yerushalayim all the days of your life.
items.text: When you ask Hashem for His blessing, think of Yerushalayim for it is the source of berachah to the world.

items.title: GRANDCHILDREN
items.he: וּרְאֵה בָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ שָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
items.quote: You will see children to your children; peace upon Yisrael.
items.text: Ask Hashem to grant you the privilege of seeing worthy grandchildren in your lifetime and they be permitted to live in a peaceful world.

129.title: A Nation in Pain
129.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: HISTORY OF PAIN
items.he: רַבַּת צְרָרוּנִי מִנְּעוּרַי
items.quote: They have been tormenting me for a long time, from my youth.
items.text: Put your anguish in a historical context. Remind yourself that Hashem rescued you in the past. Surely He will do so again.

items.he: ה’ צַדִּיק קִצֵּץ עֲבוֹת רְשָׁעִים
items.quote: Hashem is righteous; He cuts the ropes of the resha’im.

items.title: TURN THEM BACK
items.he: יֵבֹשׁוּ וְיִסֹּגוּ אָחוֹר כֹּל שֹׂנְאֵי צִיּוֹן
items.quote: Let them be shamed and turned back, all who hate Tzion.
items.text: Ask Hashem to demoralize the enemy so that they no longer have the heart to persecute us.

items.title: GREETING
items.he: בִּרְכַּת ה’ אֲלֵיכֶם
items.quote: Hashem’s blessing upon you.
items.text: You may greet another Jew with a prayer to Hashem to bless him.

items.raw: [129:8] – בֵּרַכְנוּ אֶתְכֶם בְּשֵׁם ה‘ – “We bless you in the Name of Hashem.”

130.title: From the Depths
130.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as tefillos expressing your gratitude to Hashem and as tehillos expressing your recognition of Hashem.

items.title: FROM THE DEPTHS
items.he: מִמַּעֲמַקִּים קְרָאתִיךָ ה’
items.quote: From the depths I have called You, Hashem.
items.text: Approach your tefillah to Hashem with great humility, acknowledging your unworthiness.

items.he: אֲדֹ־נָי שִׁמְעָה בְקוֹלִי, תִּהְיֶינָה אָזְנֶיךָ קַשֻּׁבוֹת לְקוֹל תַּחֲנוּנָי
items.quote: My L-rd hear my voice. May Your ears be attentive to the sound of my pleas.

items.title: FORGIVENESS
items.he: אִם עֲוֹנוֹת תִּשְׁמָר יָ־הּ אֲדֹ־נָי מִי יַעֲמֹד
items.quote: If You, O G-d, kept iniquities, O my L-rd who could survive.
items.text: Ask Hashem to grant His forgiveness for your sins and at the same time thank Him for the opportunity to do teshuvah and be forgiven.

items.he: כִּי עִמְּךָ הַסְּלִיחָה לְמַעַן תִּוָּרֵא
items.quote: Because forgiveness is with You so that You be held in reverence.

items.title: HOPE
items.he: קִוִּיתִי ה’ קִוְּתָה נַפְשִׁי וְלִדְבָרוֹ הוֹחָלְתִּי
items.quote: I have put my hope in Hashem. My soul has been hoping. I look expectantly for His word [to be fulfilled].
items.text: Declare your total commitment to Hashem and your dependence on His kindness.

items.he: נַפְשִׁי לַאדֹ־נָי מִשֹּׁמְרִים לַבֹּקֶר שֹׁמְרִים לַבֹּקֶר
items.quote: My soul [yearns] for my L-rd [more than] the watchers for the dawn watch for the dawn.

items.title: KINDNESS
items.he: כִּי עִם ה’ הַחֶסֶד וְהַרְבֵּה עִמּוֹ פְדוּת
items.quote: With Hashem there is kindness, and with Him abundant redemption.
items.text: Praise Hashem for His qualities of kindness and forgiveness of sin.

items.he: וְהוּא יִפְדֶּה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכֹּל עֲוֹנֹתָיו
items.quote: And so He will surely redeem Yisrael from all its iniquities.

131.title: To be Worthy of Redemption
131.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah to Hashem.

items.title: HUMILITY
items.he: לֹא גָבַהּ לִבִּי וְלֹא רָמוּ עֵינַי
items.quote: Hashem, my heart has not been conceited, nor have my eyes looked with superiority.
items.text: Make a conscious effort to develop and maintain humility.

items.title: SUBMISSIVENESS
items.he: אִם לֹא שִׁוִּיתִי וְדוֹמַמְתִּי נַפְשִׁי כְּגָמֻל עֲלֵי אִמּוֹ
items.quote: I swear I have calmed and stilled myself, like a nursing baby on its mother.
items.text: Work on your attitude of submissiveness to the will of Hashem, modeling it on that of a nursing baby.

items.title: HOPE
items.he: יַחֵל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל ה’ מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם
items.quote: Let Yisrael look expectantly for Hashem from this time and forever.
items.text: Having developed the right middos you are justified in hoping expectantly for the Geulah.

132.title: To Keep the Promise
132.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah to Hashem.

items.title: DAVIDIC REIGN
items.he: זְכוֹר ה’ לְדָוִד אֵת כָּל עֻנּוֹתוֹ
items.quote: O Hashem, remember for David all his anguish.
items.text: When you say the tefillah אֶת צֶֽמַח דָּוִד – in the daily Shemoneh Esrei, have in mind that you are helping fulfill David’s request and Hashem’s promise.

items.he: נִשְׁבַּע ה’ לְדָוִד אֱמֶת לֹא יָשׁוּב מִמֶּנָּה
items.quote: Hashem has sworn to David, a truth from which He will never retreat: From the fruit of your loin. I will place [him] on a throne for you.

items.title: COMMITMENT
items.he: אִם אֶתֵּן שְׁנַת לְעֵינָי לְעַפְעַפַּי תְּנוּמָה
items.quote: I will not allow restful sleep to my eyes [or] a nap to my eyelids.
items.text: Follow David’s example by dedicating yourself to a worthy goal. If you sacrifice sleep and comfort to pursue it, you are being especially virtuous.

notes: In Mizmor 132, David has provided us with a tefillah with which we can ask Hashem to remember David’s intense dedication in preparing for the Bais Hamikdash. With this tefillah we can ask Hashem to preserve the House of David forever. Was David self-conscious about enlisting our support for the glory of his own royal line? Such a tefillah could only have been written by someone who has completely overcome selfish pride and arrogance. In fact, that was precisely the theme of Mizmor 131, which serves as an introduction to Mizmor 132.

That is why it is significant that in this mizmor we ask Hashem to grant our plea “for the sake of David Your servant” (verse 9). David identified himself as a servant of Hashem, which meant that everything he did was at the direction of his Master and was intended only to please his Master, without any personal agenda mixed in. It was not a matter of his own glory. He knew it was Hashem’s will that the House of David be forever associated with the House of Hashem.

This is a challenge which is faced by everyone in a position of leadership or power over others. He must ensure that his motivations are pure and that if he ascends to a high position, he must focus on doing Hashem’s will without thoughts of personal advantage.

133.title: Brotherly Love
133.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah to Hashem.

items.title: PEACE
items.he: הִנֵּה מַה טּוֹב וּמַה נָּעִים שֶׁבֶת אַחִים גַּם יָחַד
items.quote: See now, how good and how pleasant it is, brothers dwelling together in unity.
items.text: Make a conscious effort to promote peace and goodwill among Jews.

items.title: FLOW
items.he: כַּשֶּׁמֶן הַטּוֹב עַל הָרֹאשׁ יֹרֵד עַל הַזָּקָן
items.quote: Like the fine oil on the head, flowing down upon the beard.
items.text: Ask Hashem to grant you and your loved ones a continuing flow of blessings.

items.he: כְּטַל חֶרְמוֹן שֶׁיֹּרֵד עַל הַרְרֵי צִיּוֹן כִּי שָׁם צִוָּה ה’ אֶת הַבְּרָכָה
items.quote: like the dew of [Mount] Chermon, which descends upon the mountains of Tzion, for there Hashem has commanded the blessing.

items.title: LIFE
items.he: חַיִּים עַד הָעוֹלָם
items.quote: [May there be] life forever.
items.text: Ask Hashem to grant you and your loved ones eternal life in the World to Come.

notes: This mizmor speaks of the flow of Hashem’s blessings (berachos) as being comparable to the flow of anointing oil. A thoughtful reader has brought to my attention the relationship between the root נזל, meaning “flow,” and the word “mazal.” So when we wish someone Mazal Tov, we are offering a tefillah that the flow of berachah from Hashem to that person should continue, get stronger and wash over them, and that it should continue to spread to all those around them. The contellations of stars are also referred to as מזלות, because the flow of blessing to the Jewish people is directed by Hashem from on high. Of course, that flow is not arbitrary, but reflects His will and our own deeds. It is surely not a matter of “luck”.

134.title: Exaltation
134.intro: Listed below are some of the thoughts you might have in mind when you say the words of the mizmor as a tefillah to Hashem.

items.title: BLESSING
items.he: הִנֵּה בָּרֲכוּ אֶת ה’ כָּל עַבְדֵי ה’ הָעֹמְדִים בְּבֵית ה’ בַּלֵּילוֹת
items.quote: And now bless Hashem all servants of Hashem, who stand in the House of Hashem in the nights.
items.text: Join your fellow Jews in publicly thanking and praising Hashem in His house. You will absorb the kedushah of all those present and this will result in a flow of blessing to Hashem, a flow that will never end.

items.he: שְׂאוּ יְדֵכֶם קֹדֶשׁ וּבָרֲכוּ אֶת ה’
items.quote: Raise your hands in holiness and bless Hashem.
items.text: Raising your hands symbolizes your recognition of Hashem in tefillah.

items.he: יְבָרֶכְךָ ה’ מִצִּיּוֹן עֹשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ
items.quote: May Hashem bless you from Tzion, [for He is] Maker of heaven and earth.
items.text: The blessings from Hashem originate in Tzion, representing the Torah. Through tefillah and the learning of Torah, the flow of blessing is created and enhanced.
